questions.stem: In a series LCR circuit, resonance occurs at a frequency $f_0$. If the capacitance of the capacitor is made 4 times its initial value without changing the inductance, the new resonant frequency will be:
questions.solution:
The resonant frequency is given by $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$.
When $C' = 4C$, the new frequency is:
$f' = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L(4C)}} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}\right) = \frac{f_0}{2}$.

questions.stem: In a series LCR circuit, the resonance frequency is $200\ \mathrm{rad/s}$. If the inductance of the inductor is $5\ \mathrm{H}$ and resistance is $10\ \Omega$, the quality factor $Q$ of the circuit is _________.
questions.solution:
The quality factor of a series LCR circuit is given by $Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}$.
Given $\omega_0 = 200\ \mathrm{rad/s}$, $L = 5\ \mathrm{H}$, and $R = 10\ \Omega$.
$Q = \frac{200 \times 5}{10} = 100$.

questions.stem: An AC source is rated $220\ \mathrm{V}, 50\ \mathrm{Hz}$. The average voltage of this source over any half cycle can be:
questions.solution:
The peak voltage is $V_0 = \sqrt{2} V_{\mathrm{rms}} = 220\sqrt{2}\ \mathrm{V}$.
The average voltage over a half-cycle starting from zero is $V_{\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{2V_0}{\pi} = \frac{440\sqrt{2}}{\pi}\ \mathrm{V}$. Over the other half, it is $-\frac{440\sqrt{2}}{\pi}\ \mathrm{V}$.

questions.stem: In a series LCR resonance circuit, if the value of inductance $L$ is doubled and capacitance $C$ is halved, the resonant frequency will:
questions.solution:
The resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit is given by $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.
If $L' = 2L$ and $C' = C/2$, then the new resonant frequency is:
$\omega_0' = \frac{1}{\sqrt{(2L)(C/2)}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \omega_0$.
Thus, the resonant frequency remains unchanged.

questions.stem: In a series $LCR$ circuit, the resonant frequency is $800	ext{ Hz}$. The half-power points are obtained at frequencies $740	ext{ Hz}$ and $860	ext{ Hz}$. The quality factor ($Q$-factor) of the circuit, rounded off to two decimal places, is:
questions.solution:
The bandwidth $\Delta f = f_2 - f_1 = 860 - 740 = 120	ext{ Hz}$.
The quality factor is $Q =  rac{f_r}{\Delta f} =  rac{800}{120} =  rac{20}{3} ≈ 6.67$.

questions.stem: In a series LCR resonance circuit, if the value of inductance $L$ is doubled and capacitance $C$ is halved, the resonant frequency will:
questions.solution:
Resonant frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.
New frequency $\omega_0' = \frac{1}{\sqrt{(2L)(C/2)}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \omega_0$.
Thus, the resonant frequency remains unchanged.

questions.stem: An AC source of variable frequency is connected across a series LCR circuit with $L = 10 \mathrm{mH}$, $C = 1 \mu\mathrm{F}$, and $R = 100 \Omega$. The source frequency (in $\mathrm{rad/s}$) at which the current in the circuit is maximum is $\omega_0 = 10^x \mathrm{rad/s}$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
Maximum current occurs at resonance frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$.
Given $L = 10^{-2} \mathrm{H}$ and $C = 10^{-6} \mathrm{F}$.
$\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-2} \times 10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-8}}} = 10^4 \mathrm{rad/s}$.
Comparing with $10^x$, we find $x = 4$.
